name: Debby Clark
fact: Her full name was Deborah Kelly Clark, of Bowling Green, and she read Administrative Services. In November 1973, a 21-year-old senior, she was one of twenty Kentucky college students chosen as legislative interns for the 1974 session of the General Assembly, picked from three Western applicants by campus coordinator Dr Joseph Uveges. She asked for the Judiciary or Natural Resources committee, took 15 hours of academic credit for the work, lived in Frankfort from 7 January to 24 May and was paid $300 a month. The Herald names her an Associated Student Government and Chi Omega member; the 1974 Talisman has her as mistress of ceremonies of Chi Omega's November Nonsense, posed as Old Mother Goose, and first in the front row of the Sigma Chi membership photograph.

src.label: College Heights Herald 53:20, 6 Nov 1973, p. 2; 1974 Talisman pp. 259, 283, 350

name: Debby Clark
fact: The two Deborah Clarks of the 1974 senior grid are settled. The back index of the 1974 Talisman gives them as Clark, Deborah Janca 248, 311, 350 and Clark, Deborah Kelly 259, 283, 350; the grid on p. 350 prints them as DEBORAH J. CLARK, Elem. Ed., Campbellsville and DEBORAH K. CLARK, Admin. Services, Bowling Green. Chi Omega is p. 259, so the Chi Omega Debby Clark is Deborah Kelly. Deborah Janca Clark has no ASG or Chi Omega page anywhere in the volume.

name: David Arvin
fact: The Senior Class Officers caption on p. 238 of the 1967 Talisman confirms the office the archive records for him: Judy Bertram, Treasurer; Jim Cobb, Vice President; Ronnie Sutton, Adviser; Winky Menser, President; David Arvin, Representative-at-Large; Rhea Lazarus, Adviser; Margaret Siddens, Secretary. His senior entry on the facing page gives Biology and Pembroke, the same home town the 1968 volume gives for Malcolm T. Arvin.

name: Steve Reeves
fact: The back index of the 1968 Talisman enters him as Reeves, Steve W., 291, and the junior grid on that page gives his home town as Bowling Green. He is the only Steve or Stephen Reeves in the volume, which separates him from Dennis Reeves, who sat in the Associated Students the year before.

src.label: 1968 Talisman, p. 291 and back index p. 391

name: Harold Northam
fact: He was still in the Associated Students in 1968-69, a year after the sophomore class representative term the archive records. The group caption on p. 95 of the 1969 Talisman names him third in the back row, between Phil Myers and Steve Stephens.

name: Paul Civils
fact: He was already in the Associated Students in 1968-69, a year before the sophomore representative-at-large term the archive records, and is named first in the second row of the group photograph on p. 95 of the 1969 Talisman.

name: Steve Todd
fact: He sat on the Associated Students Judicial Council in 1968-69, a year before the representative-at-large term the archive records, with Mark Skillern, Carolyn Cash, Lonnie Jackson, Russell Vertner and Brent Hall.

name: Dennis Jaffee
fact: The 1968 Talisman spells his surname Jaffe with one e, in the Student Activities Committee caption on p. 155 where he sits with Carol Bass, Ron Beck and Thelma Lee. The archive carries Jaffee. Flagged, not resolved.

name: Larry Ashby
fact: The 1968 Talisman calls the body the Judicial Council rather than the Judicial Committee, and gives its full membership as Mark Skillern, Bruce Dalrymple, Bob Matthews, Larry Ashby, Dan Leeper and Joe Glowacki. A separate James Ashby, of Russellville, reading mathematics, appears in the 1967 senior grid and is not him.

name: Susan Streible
fact: She sat on the Associated Students Executive Committee in 1967-68 as well as in the body itself, with Larry Heishman, Bill Straeffer, Claudia Fowler, Tom Evans, William Menser and Ron Beck.

name: David Bass
fact: The Talisman's ASG spread names the 1977-78 executive: president Bob Moore, activities vice president David Bass, secretary Sharon May and vice president Cathy Murphy. The 1978 back index enters him as Bass, David Eugene, 34, and gives him no class portrait page in any digitised volume from 1977 to 1981.

name: Mark Chesnut
fact: The 1981 back index enters him as Chesnut, Mark Cameron, 234, and p. 234 is the printed list of intramural champions, not a photograph. He has no class portrait page in the 1979, 1980 or 1981 index. A William George Chesnut II of Berea, unrelated to the treasurer as far as the volume shows, is the Chesnut who appears in the 1981 portrait grids.

name: David Young
fact: The 1979 back index enters him as Young, David Paul, 289, and gives him no other page. Page 289 is a text article on ASG's year with no photograph of him; the only pictures on it are of ASG newsletters on a floor and of a bloodmobile donor.

name: Alice Wicks
fact: She has no class portrait in any digitised Talisman. The back indexes give her one page each and both are the same thing: Wicks, Alice Elizabeth 263 in 1977 and 334 in 1978, each the Alpha Delta Pi membership photograph, whose sixty-odd faces cannot be read against the caption's four named rows. The 1979, 1980 and 1981 indexes give her no page at all. The Herald of 13 April 1978 reports her winning an oratorical contest with Dennis Payne, but the item on p. 7 is four paragraphs of text with no photograph.

src.label: 1977 Talisman p. 263; 1978 Talisman p. 334; College Heights Herald, 13 Apr 1978, p. 7

name: Paul Palmer
fact: The 1976 back index gives him one page, 63, and it is the printed ASG Attendance Roll effective 6 April 1976, a table of names and meetings missed. It records Paul Palmer as having missed five. Howard Sypher (four) and Scott Taylor (four) are in the same table, which is the only place in the 1976 volume that carries all three. It is text, not a photograph.

name: Scott Taylor
fact: Neither the 1974 to 1978 back indexes nor the grids carry a Scott Taylor. His only appearances are the 1976 ASG attendance roll on p. 63, where he is recorded as having missed four meetings, and the Pi Kappa Alpha membership caption on p. 288 of the same volume.
